Water boils at **100°C** (212°F) at sea level, which corresponds to standard atmospheric pressure of 1 atmosphere (about 101.3 kPa or 14.7 psi).

This is actually the basis for the historical definition of the Celsius scale: 0°C was set as the freezing point of water, and 100°C as the boiling point, both at standard atmospheric pressure.
